events.text: Pick-up today: Nissan Almera and Honda CR-V for Visiting team: Kruger outreach

text.text:
Hi Thandi 👋

Your booking *Visiting team: Kruger outreach* starts today: *Nissan Almera* (DEMO 1 GP) and *Honda CR-V* (DEMO 2 GP). As the person who booked, you’re the point person for the vehicles until they’re back.

*TODAY*

1. *Arrange the pick-up time* with the Vehicle Coordinator (pick-ups are between 07:00 and 17:00): Pieter Coordinator, +27 00 000 0000
2. *Bring every driver’s driver’s licence.* Only the drivers on the booking may drive.
3. *At the handover*, walk round the vehicles with the Vehicle Coordinator and photograph anything already damaged before you drive off.
4. *Make sure every driver has the driver instructions.* We sent them to 2 of 3 drivers. *Lee Chen* has no email on the booking, so please forward them the driver instructions (below).

*WHILE YOU HAVE IT*

• Only the drivers on the booking drive.
• Anything goes wrong (a warning light, a breakdown, an accident, damage): call the Vehicle Coordinator straight away.

*RETURNING IT*

Bring the vehicles back on *Friday, 4 December, before 12:00*: washed inside and out, with a full tank, and with the return checks done. The day before, you’ll get a reminder, with the option to return it earlier.

Driver instructions (the same as the drivers received):

*🇿🇦 DRIVING IN SOUTH AFRICA*

• *We drive on the LEFT side of the road.*
• *Speed limits.* These are only guidelines; always follow the signs posted next to the road:
   • *60 km/h* in town (*30–40 km/h* in neighbourhoods)
   • *80–100 km/h* on the open road
   • *120 km/h* on national highways

*BEFORE EACH TRIP*

*1. Walk around the vehicle*
Walk slowly all the way round, about one step away. Crouch down to see the lower parts. Look for dents, scratches, cracked lights or mirrors.
📸 Photograph anything you notice *before you drive*, close up and once from further back, and send it to the Vehicle Coordinator. Then nobody can blame you for damage that was already there.

*2. Tyres (including the spare)*

• All four should look the same: round, with only a slight bulge at the bottom. If one looks flatter, have it checked before you leave.
• Look at the sides for cuts, bulges or nails. Turn the steering wheel all the way to see the inside of the front tyres.
• The correct pressure is usually on a sticker inside the driver’s door frame or the fuel flap. A petrol attendant can check and pump them.

*3. Lights*
Switch on the headlights and hazard lights and walk round: every light and indicator should work. For the brake lights, ask someone to watch while you press the brake.

*4. Windscreen, wipers and mirrors*

• No cracks in front of the driver.
• Wipers clear the glass without smearing. Test with the washer spray.
• Mirrors are clean, not cracked, and set for you.

*5. Inside the vehicle*

• *Warning lights:* when you start the engine, the lights on the dashboard come on for a few seconds and then go off. If any stay on, take a photo and send it to the Vehicle Coordinator before you go. Red = don’t drive. Orange = tell us.
• *Seat belts:* at every seat, pull the belt quickly (it should lock), let go (it should roll back in), and buckle it (it should hold).
• *Handbrake:* it should hold the vehicle still on a slope.
• *Licence disc:* the round paper disc on the windscreen must be there and not expired.
• Every driver carries their driver’s licence.

*6. Safety kit*
Check that the *red warning triangle*, the *jack*, the *wheel spanner* and the *spare wheel* are in the vehicle. You legally need the triangle in South Africa.

*7. Under the bonnet (or ask the petrol attendant)*
Only check with the engine off, on level ground. *Never open the radiator cap when the engine is hot.*

• *Oil:* pull out the dipstick (a yellow or orange loop), wipe it, push it back in, pull it out. The level should be between the two marks. Golden-brown is good. Very black means it’s due a service, so tell us. Milky means don’t drive, call the Vehicle Coordinator.
• *Coolant (“water”):* the see-through plastic tank should be between MIN and MAX.
• *Leaks:* look at the ground where the vehicle was parked. Drips of oil (black or brown) or coolant (green, pink or orange) mean tell us. Clear water under the front is normal (it’s from the aircon).

*⛽ AT THE PETROL STATION*

In South Africa an attendant fills the vehicle for you. You stay in the vehicle.

• *Nissan Almera* (DEMO 1 GP) takes *PETROL (unleaded)*. Never put in anything else.
• *Honda CR-V* (DEMO 2 GP) takes *PETROL (unleaded)*. Never put in anything else.
• Say “Diesel, full please” or “Unleaded, full please”, or give a Rand amount.
• Ask: *“Please check the oil, water and tyre pressure.”* They’ll also clean the windscreen if you ask.

*IN AN EMERGENCY*

• Pull over well off the road, switch on the hazard lights, and put the triangle 15–20 m behind the vehicle.
• Then call the Vehicle Coordinator straight away: Pieter Coordinator, +27 00 000 0000

*RETURNING THE VEHICLE*

Bring the vehicles back on *Friday, 4 December, before 12:00*: washed inside and out, with a full tank, and with the return checks done. You’ll get a reminder the day before, and the return checks that morning.

Thank you! 🙏
FFSA Fleet

  • Oil: pull out the dipstick (a yellow or orange loop), wipe it, push it back in, pull it out. The level should be between the two marks. Golden-brown is good. Very black means it’s due a service, so tell us. Milky means don’t drive, call the Vehicle Coordinator.
  • Coolant (“water”): the see-through plastic tank should be between MIN and MAX.
  • Leaks: look at the ground where the vehicle was parked. Drips of oil (black or brown) or coolant (green, pink or orange) mean tell us. Clear water under the front is normal (it’s from the aircon).

⛽ AT THE PETROL STATION

In South Africa an attendant fills the vehicle for you. You stay in the vehicle.

  • This vehicle takes DIESEL. Never put in anything else. Say “Diesel, full please” or give a Rand amount.
  • Ask: “Please check the oil, water and tyre pressure.” They’ll also clean the windscreen if you ask.

IN AN EMERGENCY

  • Pull over well off the road, switch on the hazard lights, and put the triangle 15–20 m behind the vehicle.
  • Then call the Vehicle Coordinator straight away: Pieter Coordinator, +27 00 000 0000

RETURNING THE VEHICLE

Bring the vehicle back on Monday, 7 December, before 12:00: washed inside and out, with a full tank, and with the return checks done. You’ll get a reminder the day before, and the return checks that morning.

Thank you! 🙏
FFSA Fleet

text.text:
Hi Thandi 👋

*Nissan Almera* (DEMO 1 GP) and *Honda CR-V* (DEMO 2 GP) for *Visiting team: Kruger outreach* are due back *today, before 12:00*.

*BEFORE YOU HAND IT BACK*

1. *Wash the vehicles* inside and out (vacuum the inside, clean the windows). Keep the receipt if you use a car wash.
2. *Fill the tank* with the right fuel for each vehicle.
3. 📸 Send the Vehicle Coordinator a photo of the *km reading* and *fuel gauge* on the dashboard.
4. 📸 Send photos of any *new* damage, inside or out, even small scratches or chips. Mistakes happen, and it’s much better that we know.

   • Did anything feel, sound or smell different (noises, brakes, steering pulling to one side, vibration)?
   • Did any warning light come on?
   • Did you hit any big potholes or kerbs?
   • Did anything break or stop working?
6. Check nothing is left inside (under the seats, door pockets, boot or back doors). Make sure all the keys come back. Lock it and check every door and the boot are locked.

Then hand the keys to the Vehicle Coordinator. If you can’t make 12:00, let them know as soon as possible: Pieter Coordinator, +27 00 000 0000

Thank you for looking after it! 🙏
FFSA Fleet
